# Oversized grapheme in a fixed cell

Original OPC/XML fixture generated by `tools/oversized_glyph_fixture.py` using
Python's standard library, without an editor's serializer. `native.pdf` was
exported by the reference application. The recorder uses pypdf to
retain the source/PDF hashes, text origins, baselines and PDF clipping paths.
No third-party document or font binary is distributed in the DOCX.

Eleven controls use Arial 57pt `TT` in a fixed 27pt cell between two labeled
neighbors, with zero margins. Cases cover normal/condensed/expanded spacing,
80/100/120% scaling, combined spacing/scaling, the editor's maximum 1584pt
spacing and 600% scale, and centered/right alignment. The reference application wraps every T onto
its own line at x144.02pt; the following cell remains x171.05pt. The reference application explicitly
clips glyph ink to the physical cell rectangle (27.024pt PDF width), including
oversized text. Oversized inline pictures have separate established behavior.

Relevant ECMA-376 Part 1 clauses: 17.3.2.35 (`spacing`), 17.3.2.43 (`w`),
17.3.1.13 (`jc`), 17.4.52 (`tblLayout`), 17.18.87 (`ST_TblLayoutType`). This
records the reference application's layout behavior where those declarations do not fully specify
oversized-glyph clipping; it is not a claim of a normative contradiction.

This control establishes line splitting, alignment and horizontal clipping.
Absolute vertical font metrics and full reference typography agreement are separate
requirements; recorded baselines remain available to expose those gaps.
